## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sattaputtakhādapetivatthu* ("Eater of Seven Sons", Pv 7) is a short narrative poem included in the *Petavatthu* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Centering on karmic fruition, the text demonstrates that jealousy and hatred inexorably lead to suffering in the realm of the shades (*petas*) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in four different languages [SuttaCentral].
The text is closely related to surrounding narratives in the *Petavatthu* and the broader commentarial and avadāna traditions. In the Pali tradition, its verses are embedded and explained extensively in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, with DharmaNexus detecting 69 shared passage segments [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits heavy Pali-internal text reuse with its companion piece, the *Pañcaputtakhādapetivatthu* (Pv 6), sharing an opening sequence running from segment 0.1 through 5.4, as well as recurring formulaic segments shared with the *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31), *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15), and *Saṁsāramocakapetivatthu* (Pv 13) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus further align passages of the text with narrative episodes in Sanskrit and Tibetan collections, including the Sanskrit *Avadānaśataka*, the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003), the *Vinayavastu* (D0001-3), and the *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155-2) [DharmaNexus].
